tagline.text: Bohol's largest remaining natural forest, a birdwatching destination of caves, springs and trails

location.label: Location
location.text: A limestone forest spanning eight municipalities in central-southern Bohol, including Bilar and Carmen, about 40 km east of Tagbilaran

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~2,500 (per person, based on a day trip from Tagbilaran including transport, entrance fee and meals)

children.text: Rajah Sikatuna Protected Landscape covers about 10,452 hectares and is the largest remaining natural forest on Bohol. In its limestone forest you can find more than 120 bird species, wildlife such as the tarsier, more than 100 caves and over 30 km of trails.
Rajah Sikatuna Protected Landscape is a forested area on the limestone hills of central-southern Bohol, covering about
10,452 hectares

. It lies just south of the Chocolate Hills, is described as the largest remaining tract of natural forest on Bohol, and is one of the best-known birdwatching sites in the Philippines. It spans eight municipalities, Carmen, Sierra Bullones, Garcia Hernandez, Valencia, Dimiao, Bilar, Loboc and Batuan, and its average elevation is about 400 m. The core is natural forest left on steep limestone terrain, surrounded by plantation forest, denuded hills, grassland and farmland. One source puts limestone forest at about 60 percent, grassland at about 15 percent, plantations at about 5 percent and farmland at about 10 percent.

The name comes from Datu Sikatuna, the Bohol chieftain who made a blood compact (sandugo) with the Spanish conquistador Miguel López de Legazpi in 1565. The land became a national park of about 9,023 hectares on July 10, 1987 by Proclamation No. 129, and on April 23, 2000 it was re-established by Proclamation No. 287 as a protected landscape with its present area. It is managed by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and falls under IUCN Category V (protected landscape). In other words, it is a place where inhabited land and forest are mixed, a landscape where local life and conservation go together rather than a completely closed nature reserve.

For travelers the place has two faces. One is birds and forest. The protected landscape is an Important Bird Area with more than 120 recorded species, many of them endemic to the Philippines. The streaked reed warbler and the Philippine cockatoo are mentioned as endangered, and the list includes the Philippine hawk-eagle, Visayan broadbill, Samar hornbill, Mindanao bleeding-heart and azure-breasted pitta. The other face is walking. There are more than 30 km of marked trails, more than 100 caves, a camping area and a swimming pool, and near the entrance a tunnel leads to Magsaysay Park and the Logarita spring.

The best time to explore is early in the morning, when the forest is cool. A birding guide says bird activity slows in the midday heat but that the forest remains comfortable until about 11 a.m., and reports a checklist of 127 species (52 endemic and 14 threatened). Magsaysay Park, the main starting point, is at about 400 m elevation, and most trails are well maintained, although the limestone sections are rocky and slippery. Day tours that combine it with the Loboc River cruise, the Bilar Man-Made Forest and the Chocolate Hills are common. The information here is based on Wikipedia and tourism and birding sources; entrance fees, operating hours and guide fees differ between sources, so it is safest to check local notices first.

The forest has many endemic birds, and birdwatchers come mostly in the early morning. Targets mentioned include the Visayan endemics Samar hornbill, Visayan broadbill and yellow-breasted tailorbird, as well as Steere's pitta, the Philippine trogon and silvery and rufous-lored kingfishers. The Magsaysay clearing is good for nightjars and owls right after arrival and at dusk, and the area near the Logarita turn-off is known as an early-morning spot for the Visayan broadbill. You learn about birds by sound before sight, so we recommend binoculars and a local guide. To see the rufous hornbill you are told to take a long walk to the Loboc watershed forest with a local guide. Silvery kingfishers can be seen along the river.
Bilar Peak inside the protected landscape is about

above sea level, one of the highest points on Bohol, and an observation tower is said to stand at the summit. On a clear day you are told you can see the park, the countryside, Panglao Island and even Cebu in the distance.
Marked wildlife-viewing trails extend for more than
30 km

. Routes described in the birding guide include the Brahminy–Oriole–Tarsier loop (for mixed flocks on a first morning), the Tarictic trail from the Logarita pool to the Brahminy intersection, and the path down to the Magsaysay ranger station. Trail names and routes can change locally, so check with a guide.
The limestone terrain holds more than 100 caves, where bats and swiftlets are said to live. Some may require a guide, so do not enter alone, and bring a flashlight and sturdy shoes.

Four mountain springs, Logarita, Anislag, Mabugnao and Aghuban, supply water to local communities. Close to the entrance, a tunnel leads to Magsaysay Park (in Barangay Riverside, Bilar), a ranger station and the Logarita spring. Nearby you are also told of Duangon Cold Spring and Pangas Falls.

The Philippine tarsier, long-tailed macaque, Philippine flying lemur (colugo), two civet species and the Philippine warty pig are listed as the large mammals. Many are nocturnal and hard to meet in the daytime. The birding guide says there is no malaria and few insects, but this varies by person, so bring repellent.
The protected landscape is said to have a camping area and a swimming pool. We could not confirm their condition or how to book, so ask at the local office before you go.
The Bilar Man-Made Forest, the Chocolate Hills, the Loboc River and the Tarsier Sanctuary are all close and fit into a single day. Walk the forest first and move on to the others in the afternoon.
Leave Tagbilaran and head toward Bilar.
Register at the entrance and get a map and guide information.
Walk the forest trails, listening for birds and birdwatching.
Rest near the Logarita spring and Magsaysay Park.
Have lunch and move on to the Bilar Man-Made Forest.

Birds are most active in the early morning, so start walking by 8 a.m. at the latest. The birding guide says you will see more birds by picking the key trails than by walking the whole course. It is said to take about three mornings to see nearly all the signature birds.
Walk the trails and check the path toward Bilar Peak.
After lunch, visit the nearby Bilar Man-Made Forest.
Move on to the Chocolate Hills viewpoint.
Return to Tagbilaran.
Flights run from Manila to Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG) and take about
1 hour 20 minutes
. Check airlines and schedules when you book.
From the airport to Tagbilaran takes about
30 minutes
by taxi or van.
The protected landscape is about
40 km
east of Tagbilaran. The Bilar tourism guide says it takes about
1 hour
by bus or jeepney bound for Carmen via Bilar, and Bilar is a regular stop on the Tagbilaran–Chocolate Hills route.
From Bilar, where the Loay Interior Road passes, an
8 km
road leads to the entrance. The birding guide notes that public jeepneys do not run early enough for dawn birding and recommends a car with driver or a rented motorcycle.
You can approach along the Tagbilaran–Corella–Sikatuna–Loboc road, or along the Tagbilaran East Road from Panglao.
Some day tours that combine the man-made forest, the Chocolate Hills and the Loboc River include this place, so check according to your plan.
It is an inland forest in central Bohol, so it is cooler and more humid than the coast. The trails are dirt and limestone and become slippery in the rain, so the dry season suits walking.

The birding guide names February–June as the best period, while the Bilar tourism guide gives December–April, so sources differ. Either way the dry season suits walking and birdwatching, and you should ask a guide about the timing for particular species.

items.note: Bus or van toward Bilar and Carmen

items.note: Based on restaurants in Bilar and Loboc

There is said to be no lodging or restaurant inside the protected landscape. Most travelers stay in Tagbilaran (about
1 hour
away) and go by car with a driver. Near Bilar there is a backpacker lodge that rents motorcycles, and a guesthouse at the Chocolate Hills is reported to be about
30 minutes
away. If you plan a dawn start, it is easier to book somewhere close the day before.

There is no food near the entrance, so bring water and snacks and eat in Bilar or Loboc. In Bilar there are shops selling drinks and bread in the morning, and the lunch buffet on the Loboc River cruise is widely known, so many travelers include it in their plans.
For birds the best time is right after sunrise, and if you enter when the gate is unstaffed you may be asked to pay the entrance fee on the way out.
Bring binoculars, comfortable shoes, a hat and water.
Hiring a birdwatching guide locally helps you tell birdcalls apart.
Do not enter caves without a guide, and bring a flashlight.
Insect repellent and long sleeves are useful in the forest.
Check the entrance fee and operating hours locally first.
Carry out your trash and do not feed wildlife. About three mornings are said to be enough to see most of the signature birds.
On rainy days the trails are slippery, so check the soles of your shoes.
In the Magsaysay Park clearing, the main starting point, you can reportedly hear nightjars and owls at dusk. If you plan to stay until sunset, arrange a flashlight and your way back first.
Limestone sections are rocky and slippery after rain, so wear shoes with firm soles.
Picking plants and capturing animals is generally forbidden inside protected areas. Follow local instructions for specific rules.
Entrance fees range from ₱10 to ₱150 depending on the source, and the most recent guide says ₱100, so check locally.
Caves can be flooded or slippery after rain, so go only with a guide.
Some trail sections may lack markers, so do not go deep into the forest alone.
We could not confirm the condition of the Bilar Peak tower, so check locally.
The information in this article reflects what could be verified as of 2026; check the latest announcements.
